# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("McLaughlin_2026_axicabtagene_brexucabtagene"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("McLaughlin_2026_axicabtagene_brexucabtagene"))$description`
* Article (open access): <https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.70395>

Axicabtagene ciloleucel (axi-cel) and brexucabtagene autoleucel (brexu-cel)
carry the same anti-CD19 CAR construct but are manufactured differently. Mc
Laughlin 2026 fitted one mechanism-based population model to the peripheral
blood CAR-T-cell concentrations of both products. The infused cells enter a
central CAR-T compartment that exchanges with a peripheral compartment and is
eliminated first order. After a lag time, the central cells expand first order
at a rate that falls as a latent tumour-burden compartment, initialised at the
patient's baseline sum of the product of diameters (SPD), is depleted by
second-order CAR-T killing (Figure 1, Equations 1-3):

$$\frac{dA_c}{dt} = \rho \cdot A_c \cdot I(t > t_{lag}) \cdot \frac{SPD}{SPD_{BL}} - k_{12} A_c + k_{21} A_p - k_{el} A_c$$
$$\frac{dA_p}{dt} = k_{12} A_c - k_{21} A_p \qquad \frac{dSPD}{dt} = -k_{kill} \cdot A_c \cdot SPD$$

The blood concentration is the central amount divided by an estimated scaling
factor (`vc`, 3.14 x 10^4 L; 10^6 cells/L = 1 cell/uL).

```{r load-model}
mod <- readModelDb("McLaughlin_2026_axicabtagene_brexucabtagene")
mod_ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
mod_typical <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_ui)
```

# Population

The model was developed on 473 patients with relapsed or refractory B-cell
lymphoma (Table 1 of the paper). In ZUMA-1, ZUMA-5 and ZUMA-7, 406 received
axi-cel for large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL, PMBCL, transformed FL and other),
follicular lymphoma or marginal zone lymphoma. In ZUMA-2, 67 received brexu-cel
for mantle cell lymphoma (MCL). Median age was 60 years (21-80) and median
body weight 82.7 kg (43.1-166); 35.5% were female and 87.5% White. Median
baseline SPD was 2,244 mm^2 and median baseline albumin 40 g/L. Every patient
received a single intravenous infusion at a target 2 x 10^6 CAR-T cells/kg
after cyclophosphamide/fludarabine lymphodepletion, a median of 165 x 10^6
CAR+ cells (51.8-201). The 2,785 concentrations came from qPCR and were
converted to cells/uL.

The same information is available programmatically:

```{r population}
str(mod_ui$population)
```

# Source trace

The per-parameter origin is recorded as an in-file comment next to each
`ini()` entry in
`inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/McLaughlin_2026_axicabtagene_brexucabtagene.R`.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `d/dt(central)`, `d/dt(peripheral1)`, `d/dt(tumor)` | n/a | Equations 1-3; Figure 1 |
| `tlag_ind` (expansion switch) | 0 for t <= tlag, 1 after | Equation 1 |
| `tumor(0) <- TUMSZ` | baseline SPD | Results, 'Model development' |
| `Cc <- central / vc` | n/a | Results, 'Model development' (scaling factor) |
| `lkexp_max` (rho) | log(2.70) 1/day | Table 2 |
| `lkel` | log(0.120) 1/day | Table 2 |
| `lk12` | log(0.0465) 1/day | Table 2 |
| `lk21` | log(0.0108) 1/day | Table 2 |
| `lkkill` | log(1.33e-6) 1/(day x 10^6 cells) | Table 2 |
| `ltlag` | log(2.47) day | Table 2 |
| `lvc` (scaling factor) | log(3.14e4) L | Table 2 |
| `e_wt_kel` | 0.781, on log(WT/82.7) | Table 2 and footnote a; Table 1 median |
| `e_cart_effector_t_pct_kexp_max` | -0.00619 per %, centred at 24.7% | Table 2; Table 1 median |

| `etaexpSd` | 0.545^2 | Table 2 'IIV RUV' |
| `expSd` | 0.969 | Table 2 'RUV' |

# Typical-value simulations (Figure 5)

The reference patient of Figures 4 and 5 is axi-cel in a non-MCL lymphoma,
24.7% effector T cells in the product, no prior bendamustine, 82.7 kg, 40 g/L
albumin, baseline SPD 2,244 mm^2 and 2 x 10^6 cells/kg. Each scenario below
changes one of these at a time, as the paper does. Because the expansion is
driven by the ratio `tumor / TUMSZ` and the killing is first order in tumour
burden, the typical profile does not depend on the baseline SPD value itself.

```{r tv-helpers}
ref_cov <- data.frame(
  WT = 82.7, ALB = 40, CART_EFFECTOR_T_PCT = 24.7, PRIOR_BENDAMUSTINE = 0,
  TUMTP_MCL = 0, STUDY_ZUMA7 = 0, TUMSZ = 2244
)
inf_dur <- 0.5 / 24 # 30-min infusion, in days

# One typical-value subject per scenario: `changes` is a named list of the
# covariates that differ from the reference patient, `dose_per_kg` the dose in
# 10^6 cells/kg.
make_scenario <- function(id, panel, label, changes = list(), dose_per_kg = 2, times) {
  cov <- ref_cov
  for (nm in names(changes)) cov[[nm]] <- changes[[nm]]
  amt <- dose_per_kg * cov$WT
  dose <- data.frame(id = id, time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = amt, dur = inf_dur, cmt = "central")
  obs <- data.frame(id = id, time = times, evid = 0L, amt = 0, dur = 0, cmt = "central")
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    cbind(cov[rep(1, nrow(dose) + nrow(obs)), , drop = FALSE]) |>
    dplyr::mutate(panel = panel, scenario = label)
}

scenario_defs <- list(
  list("Dose", "0.02 x 10^6 cells/kg", list(), 0.02),
  list("Dose", "0.2 x 10^6 cells/kg", list(), 0.2),
  list("Dose", "2 x 10^6 cells/kg", list(), 2),
  list("Dose", "20 x 10^6 cells/kg", list(), 20),
  list("Dose", "200 x 10^6 cells/kg", list(), 200),
  list("Product/disease type", "Axi-cel/non-MCL", list(), 2),
  list("Product/disease type", "Brexu-cel/MCL, no prior bendamustine", list(TUMTP_MCL = 1), 2),
  list("Product/disease type", "Brexu-cel/MCL, prior bendamustine", list(TUMTP_MCL = 1, PRIOR_BENDAMUSTINE = 1), 2),
  list("Body weight", "55.6 kg", list(WT = 55.6), 2),
  list("Body weight", "82.7 kg", list(), 2),
  list("Body weight", "120 kg", list(WT = 120), 2),
  list("Product %TEFF", "7.76%", list(CART_EFFECTOR_T_PCT = 7.76), 2),
  list("Product %TEFF", "24.7%", list(), 2),
  list("Product %TEFF", "55.3%", list(CART_EFFECTOR_T_PCT = 55.3), 2),
  list("Prior bendamustine", "No prior bendamustine", list(), 2),
  list("Prior bendamustine", "Prior bendamustine", list(PRIOR_BENDAMUSTINE = 1), 2),
  list("Baseline albumin", "30 g/L", list(ALB = 30), 2),
  list("Baseline albumin", "40 g/L", list(), 2),
  list("Baseline albumin", "46 g/L", list(ALB = 46), 2)
)

tv_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 28, by = 0.02), seq(28.5, 365, by = 0.5))))
tv_events <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(scenario_defs), function(i) {
  s <- scenario_defs[[i]]
  make_scenario(i, s[[1]], s[[2]], s[[3]], s[[4]], times = tv_times)
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(tv_events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

tv <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_typical,
  events = tv_events,
  keep = c("panel", "scenario")
) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r figure-5, fig.height = 8}
tv |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= 2) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Cc, colour = scenario)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(3, 10, 30, 100, 300)) +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = c(0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time since infusion (days)", y = "CAR-T cells (cells/uL)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 5 of Mc Laughlin 2026 (typical-value profiles)."
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 2))
```

The reference profile peaks at about 50 cells/uL around day 7-8, as in every panel
of Figure 5. Increasing the dose shifts the peak earlier but barely raises it;
brexu-cel in MCL peaks later and about 2.6-fold higher, and prior bendamustine
lowers and delays the peak.

```{r figure-5-check}
ref_peak <- tv |>
  dplyr::filter(scenario == "2 x 10^6 cells/kg") |>
  dplyr::slice_max(Cc, n = 1)
ref_peak[, c("time", "Cc")]
# Read off Figure 5: the reference peak sits near 50 cells/uL between day 7
# and day 9. A mistranscribed rho, scaling factor or dose unit moves it by
# far more than this window.
stopifnot(
  ref_peak$Cc > 35, ref_peak$Cc < 70,
  ref_peak$time > 6, ref_peak$time < 10
)
```

# Forest plot of covariate effects (Figure 4) with PKNCA

Figure 4 reports the median predicted Cmax and AUC0-28d of each covariate
level relative to the reference patient. PKNCA computes Cmax and AUC0-28d on
the typical-value profiles above (scenario is the grouping variable), and
the ratios to the reference patient are compared with the published medians.

```{r pknca-tv}
tv_nca <- tv |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc), time <= 28) |>
  dplyr::select(id, scenario, time, Cc)
# Guarantee a time-zero row per subject.
tv_nca <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tv_nca,
  tv_nca |> dplyr::distinct(id, scenario) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, scenario, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time)

tv_dose <- tv_events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, scenario, time, amt)

tv_data <- PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(tv_nca, Cc ~ time | scenario + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(tv_dose, amt ~ time | scenario + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 28, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
)
tv_res <- as.data.frame(PKNCA::pk.nca(tv_data))

tv_wide <- tv_res |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast")) |>
  dplyr::select(scenario, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)
ref_row <- tv_wide[tv_wide$scenario == "2 x 10^6 cells/kg", ]

# Figure 4 statistics boxes (median relative change).
fig4 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario,                              ~cmax_pub, ~auc_pub,
  "Brexu-cel/MCL, no prior bendamustine", 2.6,       2.6,
  "7.76%",                                1.1,       1.1,
  "55.3%",                                0.80,      0.83,
  "Prior bendamustine",                   0.71,      0.75,
  "55.6 kg",                              1.0,       1.2,
  "120 kg",                               0.95,      0.82,
  "30 g/L",                               0.82,      0.84,
  "46 g/L",                               1.1,       1.1
)

forest <- fig4 |>
  dplyr::left_join(tv_wide, by = "scenario") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    cmax_sim = cmax / ref_row$cmax,
    auc_sim = auclast / ref_row$auclast,
    # Half a unit of the last digit printed in Figure 4 (two significant
    # figures) plus 2%: Figure 4 shows the median ratio over 250 parameter
    # vectors drawn from the covariance matrix, which differs slightly from
    # the typical-value ratio. A wrong sign or a mistranscribed coefficient
    # moves a ratio by 10% or more.
    tol_cmax = 0.5 * 10^(floor(log10(cmax_pub)) - 1) + 0.02 * cmax_pub,
    tol_auc = 0.5 * 10^(floor(log10(auc_pub)) - 1) + 0.02 * auc_pub
  )

forest |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    "Covariate level" = scenario,
    "Cmax ratio, simulated" = signif(cmax_sim, 3),
    "Cmax ratio, Figure 4" = cmax_pub,
    "AUC0-28d ratio, simulated" = signif(auc_sim, 3),
    "AUC0-28d ratio, Figure 4" = auc_pub
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical-value exposure relative to the reference patient vs. the Figure 4 medians.")

stopifnot(
  all(abs(forest$cmax_sim - forest$cmax_pub) <= forest$tol_cmax),
  all(abs(forest$auc_sim - forest$auc_pub) <= forest$tol_auc)
)
```

Every simulated ratio agrees with the Figure 4 median to within 0.01. Three
round to a neighbouring value in the second decimal: Cmax and AUC0-28d at
55.3% effector T cells (0.79 and 0.82 against 0.80 and 0.83) and AUC0-28d at
30 g/L albumin (0.85 against 0.84). Figure 4 prints the median over sampled
parameter vectors rather than the typical-value ratio, which explains
differences of this size. The text quotes the largest effects directly: brexu-cel in MCL
gives 160% higher Cmax and AUC0-28d, and prior bendamustine 29% lower Cmax and
25% lower AUC0-28d.

# Stochastic simulation by product (Figure 2)

A virtual cohort of 200 axi-cel and 200 brexu-cel patients is drawn from the
Table 1 distributions by product. The simulated observations (with residual
error) at the protocol sampling days are summarised as the 5th, 50th and 95th
percentiles, for comparison with the observed percentiles of the pcVPC in
Figure 2. The model's censoring at the study-specific thresholds is not
applied here, so the lower percentiles at late times fall below what the
assay reported.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261025)
set.seed(20261025)

# Positive covariate drawn as log-normal from a median and a mean (Table 1),
# truncated to the observed range.
draw_lognormal <- function(n, median, mean, lo, hi) {
  sdlog <- sqrt(2 * log(mean / median))
  pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(n, log(median), sdlog)), lo), hi)
}

make_cohort <- function(n, product, id_offset) {
  is_brexu <- product == "Brexu-cel (MCL)"
  wt <- if (is_brexu) draw_lognormal(n, 80.9, 81.7, 46.3, 140) else draw_lognormal(n, 82.8, 84.7, 43.1, 166)
  teff <- if (is_brexu) draw_lognormal(n, 28.2, 29.7, 2.8, 65.2) else draw_lognormal(n, 24.7, 27.1, 1.3, 87.6)
  alb <- pmin(pmax(rnorm(n, if (is_brexu) 38 else 39.2, if (is_brexu) 5.67 else 5.12), 19), 53)
  data.frame(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n),
    product = product,
    WT = wt,
    ALB = alb,
    CART_EFFECTOR_T_PCT = teff,
    PRIOR_BENDAMUSTINE = rbinom(n, 1, if (is_brexu) 0.537 else 0.0542),
    TUMTP_MCL = as.integer(is_brexu),
    STUDY_ZUMA7 = if (is_brexu) 0L else rbinom(n, 1, 161 / 406),
    TUMSZ = if (is_brexu) draw_lognormal(n, 2158, 3280, 260, 16880) else draw_lognormal(n, 2342, 3686, 171, 34680)
  ) |>
    # Target 2 x 10^6 cells/kg, capped at the 200 x 10^6 cells of a full bag.
    dplyr::mutate(amt = pmin(2 * WT, 200))
}

cohort <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_cohort(200, "Axi-cel", 0L),
  make_cohort(200, "Brexu-cel (MCL)", 200L)
)

obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 28, by = 0.25), 56, 91, 182, 365)))
vpc_events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  cohort |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, dur = inf_dur, cmt = "central"),
  cohort |>
    dplyr::select(-amt) |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, dur = 0, cmt = "central")
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(vpc_events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_ui, events = vpc_events, keep = c("product")) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r figure-2}
nominal_days <- c(1, 3, 7, 14, 28, 91, 182, 365)
sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% nominal_days) |>
  dplyr::group_by(product, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(sim, 0.05), Q50 = median(sim), Q95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~product) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(1, 10, 100, 365)) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (days)", y = "CAR-T cells (cells/uL)",
    caption = "Compare with the observed percentiles in Figure 2 of Mc Laughlin 2026 (5th, median, 95th)."
  )
```

The simulated median rises from a few thousandths of a cell/uL on days 1-3
to tens of cells/uL at days 7-14, then falls by two to three orders of
magnitude by month 6, with a 5th-95th percentile band spanning three to four
orders of magnitude. Figure 2 shows the same
shape and spread, with ZUMA-2 (brexu-cel, MCL) peaking higher than the axi-cel
studies.

## PKNCA by product

```{r pknca-sim}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc), time <= 28) |>
  dplyr::select(id, product, time, Cc)
sim_nca <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> dplyr::distinct(id, product) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, product, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time)

sim_dose <- cohort |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0) |>
  dplyr::select(id, product, time, amt)

sim_data <- PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | product + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(sim_dose, amt ~ time | product + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 28, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
)
sim_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(sim_data)
summary(sim_res)

prod_medians <- as.data.frame(sim_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(product, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = product, values_from = median) |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = `Brexu-cel (MCL)` / `Axi-cel`)
prod_medians

# The brexu-cel/MCL cohort differs from the reference ratio of 2.6 by its
# other covariates (more prior bendamustine), and the ratio of two cohort
# medians carries sampling noise; it must stay clearly above 1.
stopifnot(all(prod_medians$ratio > 1.3), all(prod_medians$ratio < 4))
```

The paper does not tabulate Cmax or AUC0-28d by product, so there is no
published NCA to compare with. The brexu-cel cohort median is roughly two to
three times the axi-cel median, in line with the 2.6-fold typical effect in
Figure 4. With between-patient variability this large, a ratio of cohort
medians does not follow typical-value arithmetic exactly. The larger
prior-bendamustine share in the brexu-cel cohort (54% against 5%) pulls the
ratio down, and its higher effector-T-cell share and lower albumin pull it
down further, but these shifts are of the same order as the sampling noise
with 200 patients per product.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **IIV and residual SD read as sqrt(omega^2).** Table 2 gives the IIV and
  RUV values as "CV", and its footnote says their RSEs are "on the
  approximate SD scale", which is how PsN reports the square root of the
  variance. The variances in `ini()` are therefore the squares of the printed
  values (for example 1.97^2 = 3.88 for k21), not log(1 + CV^2).
- **Residual error.** Additive on the log scale (`lnorm`), with an
  exponential IIV on the residual SD and a 71.9% larger SD in ZUMA-7, as
  described in the Results and Table 2.
- **Censoring.** The authors handled 14.6% of samples reported as zero with
  the M3 method at study-specific thresholds (0.0001624-0.00744 cells/uL).
  The model file simulates uncensored concentrations; apply the thresholds
  to simulated data when comparing with observed data.
- **Covariate centring.** Continuous covariates are exponential models
  centred on the overall Table 1 medians (24.7% TEFF, 40 g/L albumin), with
  body weight log-transformed so that its effect is the power form
  `(WT/82.7)^0.781`; categorical effects are fractional changes. The Figure 4
  ratios, reproduced above, confirm these forms.
- **Brexu-cel / MCL composite.** Every brexu-cel patient had MCL and no
  axi-cel patient did, so the paper estimated one composite effect. The
  library encodes it with the MCL indicator `TUMTP_MCL`; set it to 1 to
  simulate brexu-cel in MCL. The model cannot separate the product from the
  disease.
- **Covariate names.** The maintainers ratified two new covariate columns
  for this model: `CART_EFFECTOR_T_PCT` (effector T cells, CD45RA+ CCR7-, as
  a percentage of viable CD3+ cells in the product) and `PRIOR_BENDAMUSTINE`
  (bendamustine in an earlier line of therapy, distinct from the concomitant
  `CONMED_BENDAMUSTINE`).
- **Baseline SPD.** The tumour compartment starts at the baseline SPD
  (`TUMSZ`), and the expansion depends only on `tumor / TUMSZ`. With
  first-order killing, the typical CAR-T profile is the same for any baseline
  SPD; the value matters only for the predicted latent tumour burden, which
  the authors note has not been validated against tumour measurements.
- **Infusion and dose.** Doses are 30-minute infusions into `central` in
  units of 10^6 cells, as in the paper. The virtual cohort uses 2 x 10^6
  cells/kg capped at 200 x 10^6 cells, and the covariate distributions are
  log-normal or normal draws matched to the Table 1 medians and means by
  product, truncated to the observed ranges.
- **Errata.** No correction notice for the article was found as of
  2026-11-22.
